title: Revive the dormant plugin host: opt-in wiring, publisher-signed packages, consent UX, install-from-registry
description: fe-plugin (Rhai + Wasmtime host, lifecycle, capability tokens) and fe-sdk (stable extension API, UiExtensionRegistry, ApiExtensionHandle) are complete but wired to nothing: no crate depends on fe-plugin, no host thread is spawned by fractalengine or fractalengine-relay, and even the first-party fe-terrain extension's own registration functions are never called. This track makes the plugin system real: an opt-in host thread, a publisher-signed package format (ed25519) replacing the optional BLAKE3 self-check, a capability-manifest consent UX, install-from-registry over registry protocol v1 (reusing hexon_entitlements_20261031's registry protocol and fe_format::entitlement::EntitlementVerifier for licensed plugins), and version-aligned rhai so extensions/iot-bridge can join the workspace. No business logic — this repo only describes open capability.
alignment: Realises conductor/open-core.md's S-PLUGIN seam and decision D-12 (format and engine stay open); matches conductor/roadmap.md's open-core framing. Any party (a self-hoster, an organisation, an external catalogue) may run review, counter-signing or revocation-list publishing on top of this seam; this repo never names or depends on such consumers.
depends_on: hexon_entitlements_20261031 (Phase 4 / S4 only; Phases 0-3 and 5 do not wait)

OD-7 iot-bridge workspace join + rhai alignment direction
OD-8 revocation-list transport (rec: pull from a URL configured beside each revocation-capable trust root, cache last-good list)

notes: 2026-10-31: track drafted (docs only) from the 2026-10-31 open-core grill. Inventory confirms the system is architecturally complete but entirely unwired: `fe-plugin` has zero dependents in the workspace; `fe_ui`/the two binaries never construct `PluginRegistry` or `UiExtensionRegistry` as Bevy resources; `fe-terrain/src/extension.rs::register_terrain_ui` and `fe-terrain/src/api_ext.rs::terrain_api_routes` have zero call sites outside their own unit tests (verified via `git grep -n register_terrain_ui` / `terrain_api_routes` — only the defining files match).

2026-10-31: folded in verified findings from a sibling research session on 'can a plugin act as a P2P/NAT relay?' (1) NO by design: `network_scope`/`external_http` are parsed into `CapabilityManifest`/`CapabilityToken` (fe-plugin/src/capability.rs:34-39,73-76) but nothing in the workspace enforces them except one dead-end match arm (capability.rs:173-181, `CapabilityOperation::HttpRequest`) that is itself never constructed by any caller — recorded as OD-1 with recommended default 'enforce deny-by-default, no grant path in v1'. (2) The WIT world (`fe-plugin/wit/hexon-plugin.wit:124-128`) imports `node-api`/`plugin-log`/`query-api`, but `fe-plugin/src/AGENTS.md:131` calls it an 'aspirational contract, not the wired ABI' (the real host registers core-ABI `func_wrap` imports in `wasm/host_imports.rs`, no bindgen) — recorded as OD-2, must be reconciled before any third-party publishing claim. (3) The iroh `Endpoint` lives entirely inside the sync thread (fe-sync); P2P/relay behavior is explicitly a non-goal for plugins in this track — that question is answered and closed, not left open; relay advertising is the public relay_operability_20261031 track's S-RELAY-ADVERTISE seam.

2026-10-31: fresh-context review fixes — (1) S1 also owns fe-api/src/server.rs: fe-api/src/rest.rs only holds handlers, routes are registered in build_router; (2) one revocation model with hexon_entitlements_20261031: the signed revocation list is a package-level kill switch keyed by (package_id, content_hash), accepted only from trust roots marked for revocation; licence revocation for licensed plugins is token expiry + refused reissuance (S-ENTITLEMENT), never this list; (3) install-from-registry checks the registry's X-Hexon-Registry-Protocol header / /health protocol_version before fetching; (4) fe-plugin/Cargo.toml line cites corrected in spec.md (fe-sdk :12, rhai :14, wasmtime :15).

Phase 1: host thread wired behind opt-in feature+runtime flag (mirrors FE_API_SCREENSHOT_ALLOW idiom); close OD-1 (enforce or strip network_scope/external_http) in the SAME phase; wire fe-ui to actually construct UiExtensionRegistry and call fe_terrain::extension::register_terrain_ui; mount fe-terrain's ApiExtensionHandle routes in fe-api

Phase 2: publisher-signed package format — ed25519 signature over (manifest bytes || payload hash) replacing lifecycle.rs's optional BLAKE3 self-check; configurable trust roots (OD-3); unsigned refused unless an explicit dev flag; new trust-root/revocation-list consumer module
Phase 3: capability-manifest consent UX in fe-ui — modal listing requested verse/petal/property scope, named capabilities, and network_scope before Install is enabled

Phase 4: install-from-registry over registry protocol v1 — check the registry's protocol version (X-Hexon-Registry-Protocol header / /health protocol_version), fetch, verify signature (S2), refuse anything on a trusted revocation list, verify entitlement via fe_format::entitlement::EntitlementVerifier for LicenseType::Paid packages (enables fe-format's entitlement feature), activate
Phase 5: extensions/iot-bridge joins the root workspace; align rhai version (fe-plugin pins 1.19, iot-bridge pins 1.24) to one version across host + example
Review-and-fix (opus, fresh context): /code-review high AND mandatory /security-review (sandbox, signatures, untrusted-code execution, capability enforcement) — fixes its own findings

tripwires: the opt-in flag is the security boundary while wasmtime advisories are triaged-not-fixed — default OFF in every build config, including CI
OD-1 (network_scope/external_http enforcement) must close in S1, never deferred — a live host with a parsed-but-unchecked network capability is a silent gap, not a TODO
unsigned packages refused by default; the dev-flag escape hatch must never be reachable from a release build
no pricing, revenue, payment, or marketplace business logic in ANY file this track touches — PUBLIC repo, open capability only
a revocation list is accepted only when signed by a trust-root entry marked for revocation; a key trusted only to sign packages can never revoke someone else's package
WIT (fe-plugin/wit/hexon-plugin.wit) and wasm/host_imports.rs must not diverge silently — every WIT edit gets a matching host_imports.rs change or an explicit UNSTABLE marker (OD-2)
agents never run cargo; orchestrator gates once per wave
